report.tagline: PayPal's US app for sending money to friends, with a social feed of payments, now growing into a debit card and online checkout.
report.simpleSummary: Venmo is how many Americans split dinner, rent or a cab with friends. You send money with a phone number or username, add an emoji note, and friends can see a feed of who paid whom (not the amount). Sending money from your bank or balance is free. Venmo earns money when you want cash instantly, when you pay a business, or when you use its debit or credit card.

overview.whatItDoes: Venmo lets people in the US send and receive money with friends in seconds and shows a social feed of payments. It now also offers a debit card, a credit card, 'Pay with Venmo' at online stores, business profiles for small sellers, and crypto. PayPal is using it to turn free friend payments into paid shopping and card spending.
howItWorks: You download the app, link a bank account or debit card and pick a username.
You pay a friend by name, phone number or QR code and add a note, often an emoji.
Money lands in the friend's Venmo balance; moving it to the bank is free in 1 to 3 days or 1.75% instantly.
Payments show on a feed to friends, unless set to private.
Businesses and sellers pay 1.9% plus 10 cents for goods and services payments.
The Venmo Debit Card and Pay with Venmo let people spend their balance in shops and online.
overview.valueProposition: For users: the easiest way to pay back friends, with a bit of fun. For PayPal: a young, active user base who keep money in Venmo and can be turned into shoppers and card users.

businessModel.summary: Friend payments are free, so Venmo earns from things around them: instant transfers, business payments, card spending, Pay with Venmo, and interest on balances.

revenueStreams.detail: 1.75% to move money to a bank right away.
1.9% plus 10 cents on goods and services.
Fees from merchants when users spend with Venmo cards.
Interest on money held and spreads on crypto trades.

businessModel.pricing: Sending from bank, debit card or balance: free. Sending with a credit card: 3%. Instant transfer to bank: 1.75% (min $0.25, max $25). Goods and services seller fee: 1.9% plus 10 cents. Standard bank transfer: free.
businessModel.unitEconomics: A typical user sending $200 a month to friends costs Venmo a little to process and earns it almost nothing. If that user does two instant transfers of $300 a month, Venmo earns about $10.50. If they spend $300 a month on the debit card, Venmo might earn about $3 to $4 in interchange. So average revenue is roughly $25 to $30 per active user a year, and Venmo makes money only when users cash out fast, shop or use cards.

howTheyGetUsers: Network effect: you join because friends ask you to pay them on Venmo
Social feed shows Venmo to friends

Referral bonuses and debit card offers
whatBringsUsersBack: Shared costs like rent and dinners

growth.moat: Venmo's moat is its network effect: in many US friend groups, Venmo is the default, and the username is how people pay each other. A new app has to get whole friend groups to switch at once.

competitors.name: Zelle
competitors.positioning: Bank-owned instant transfers inside bank apps.

competitors.name: Cash App

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Venmo is stronger with college students and friend groups; Cash App is stronger with lower-income users and banking.

competitors.name: Apple Cash
competitors.positioning: Payments in iMessage and Apple Wallet.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Venmo works on any phone and has a feed.

competitors.name: PayPal

competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Venmo targets young US users and social payments.

pmLessons: A free core product can create a strong network, but you must design paid actions around it.
Social features help a payments app spread, but bring privacy costs.
Speed is something people will pay for: instant transfer is a big earner.
Owning the balance (money in the app) is key to earning more from users.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you make more money from Venmo without charging for friend payments?

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Venmo with UPI apps like PhonePe.
interviewQuestions.hint: UPI is free and bank-to-bank; Venmo holds a balance and earns from cash-out and cards.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Venmo keep its public feed?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh growth and fun against privacy; consider defaults and data.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you cut scams on Venmo?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map scam types, add friction for risky payments, use data, measure scam rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Venmo?
interviewQuestions.hint: Monthly active accounts sending or spending; explain drivers.
